correctness.rationale: First Lanczos Ritz value equals Gaussian Rayleigh quotient, hence signed bias B=n E_w log(sum_i w_i exp(x_i))−sum_i x_i, w~Dirichlet(1/2,...,1/2). Jensen gives B>=0; strict separate convexity ∂²_i B=nE[p_i(1−p_i)]>0 forces all worst spectra to endpoints 1,κ (no interior extremizer). Endpoint sums T~Beta(j/2,(n−j)/2) give exact B_j. For n=2, integrate arcsine to obtain 4logcosh(logκ/4). Beta moments give small-δ tie-breaking to j=floor(n/2), and dominated convergence/digamma gives high-κ unique j=1. Independent SciPy beta quadratures for n=2,4,5 at representative κ confirmed closed n2 formula and near/far multiplicity crossover.
correctness.residual_risks: Finite quadrature is supporting, not proof of convex extreme spectra or all conditioning regimes; only one Gaussian probe and one node, expected signed error.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader stochastic Lanczos/Hutch++ and trace-estimation bounds address algorithms and high-probability or multistep errors. They do not explicitly dominate the sharp one-node expectation-bias maximum over all n-dimensional SPD spectra with condition number<=kappa.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge: strict coordinatewise convexity identifies exact worst-case one-node Gaussian Lanczos expected logdet bias by a max over beta integrals, with conditioning-dependent unique extremal multiplicity. The full-text accessible 2026 Mbingui–Tambue–Karambal stochastic Krylov preprint develops Lanczos/Hutch++ trace error bounds and algorithms, not the inspected condition-number-sharp one-node expectation law. The related single-probe paper considers multiple nodes. Priority risk remains from classical Jensen/Dirichlet logsumexp extremal literature.
residual_risks: Equivalent sharp Dirichlet/Jensen-gap eigenvalue optimization might have appeared in classical matrix inequalities, even if not indexed under Lanczos.
No claim about one-node variance, tail concentration, floating-point arithmetic, non-Gaussian probes, or multistep quadrature.

value.rationale: The least expensive nontrivial stochastic Lanczos log-determinant rule has a natural, previously unquantified worst systematic overestimate at a fixed spectral condition number; the exact finite-dimensional upper envelope and shift from balanced to singleton spikes provide sharp calibration and conceptual information about bias regimes.

limitations: Only real SPD matrices n>=2, condition<=κ, one standard Gaussian probe and one Lanczos node, expected signed bias.
